shared.moneyUnit: Amount shown in euros. Prices are not converted: for an asset listed in dollars, the amount is actually in dollars.
shared.marketMoneyUnit: Amount shown in dollars. Prices are not converted: for an asset listed in another currency (e.g. in euros on Euronext), the value is actually in its listing currency.
shared.twr: The engine chains the portfolio’s performance day after day, measured before the day’s contribution: a monthly contribution is not counted as performance (time-weighted return, TWR).

finalValue.title: Final value
finalValue.purpose: What the portfolio is worth on the last day of the period: the amount you would get by selling everything that day, before selling fees.
finalValue.computation: Sum, for each asset, of the quantity held multiplied by its last known closing price. Fees already paid are deducted, since they reduced the quantities bought.
finalValue.formula: final value = Σ quantity(asset) × price(asset, last day)
finalValue.readingTip: Compare it with the amount invested: the difference between the two is the profit.

profit.title: Profit
profit.purpose: The gain (or loss) in euros, once everything you paid in is subtracted.
profit.computation: Final value minus total amount invested.
profit.unit: {moneyUnit} Negative in case of a loss.

totalInvested.title: Amount invested
totalInvested.purpose: All the money that left your pocket: initial capital and, with DCA, each contribution.
totalInvested.computation: Sum of the contributions, fees included: a €6,000 order costs €6,000, fees included. Rebalancing is self-financing and does not increase it.

priceReturn.title: Return excluding dividends
priceReturn.purpose: Isolate what prices alone return, to measure what dividends add.
priceReturn.computation: The engine replays the simulation paying no dividend. The gap with the total return comes from the reinvested dividends.
priceReturn.formula: dividend contribution = total return − return excluding dividends
priceReturn.readingTip: Equal to the total return when the holdings pay nothing.

dividendTotal.title: Dividends received
dividendTotal.purpose: See how much the holdings paid in dividends, already put back into the portfolio.
dividendTotal.computation: On each ex-dividend date, the dividend per share is multiplied by the shares held. That amount is bought back at that day's price, with no fee. Dollar dividends are converted to euros at the day's rate.
dividendTotal.formula: dividends = Σ shares held × dividend per share
dividendTotal.readingTip: They are already included in the final value and the total return.

fxContribution.title: Currency effect
fxContribution.purpose: Understand the share of the return due to the euro moving against the currency of the holdings.
fxContribution.computation: The engine replays the simulation in local currency, without conversion, then subtracts that return from the return in euros.
fxContribution.formula: currency effect = return in euros − return in local currency
fxContribution.unit: Ratio points displayed as a percentage.
fxContribution.readingTip: +3%: the dollar added 3 points of return against the euro. A dollar stock can gain in price and lose in euros.

localPriceReturn.title: Price return in local currency
localPriceReturn.purpose: See what prices alone return, before dividends and before conversion to euros.
localPriceReturn.computation: The engine replays the simulation with no dividend, with prices in their trading currency, without conversion.
localPriceReturn.readingTip: Differs from the return excluding dividends in euros when a holding trades in dollars: the currency effect is not counted yet.

dividendContribution.title: Contribution of reinvested dividends
dividendContribution.purpose: Measure what reinvested dividends add to the price return.
dividendContribution.computation: Local-currency return with dividends, minus local-currency return without dividends.
dividendContribution.formula: contribution = local return with dividends − local return without dividends
dividendContribution.unit: Ratio points displayed as a percentage.
dividendContribution.readingTip: +1.2 pt: reinvested dividends added 1.2 points to the return.

localReturn.title: Return in local currency
localReturn.purpose: See the return before the currency effect: prices and dividends, without conversion to euros.
localReturn.computation: The engine replays the simulation with prices in their trading currency, dividends reinvested.
localReturn.readingTip: Adding the currency effect gives the return in euros.

dividendGain.title: Gap due to dividends
dividendGain.purpose: Know how much reinvested dividends earned in euros over the period.
dividendGain.computation: Final value of the portfolio minus the final value of the same portfolio without reinvested dividends. The reinvested shares grew with prices too: the gap exceeds the total received.
dividendGain.formula: gap = final value − final value without dividends
dividendGain.readingTip: Higher than the dividends received when the shares bought back gained value.

dividendAmount.title: Dividend amount
dividendAmount.purpose: See how much a payment returned on the ex-dividend date.
dividendAmount.computation: Shares held on the ex-date multiplied by the dividend per share, converted to euros at that day's rate, rounded to the cent.
dividendAmount.formula: amount = shares held × dividend per share
dividendAmount.readingTip: Taxes and withholding are not included.

dividendQuantity.title: Shares bought back
dividendQuantity.purpose: See how many shares the dividend added to the portfolio.
dividendQuantity.computation: Dividend amount divided by the ex-date closing price, with no fee. Shares are fractional.
dividendQuantity.unit: Number of shares, up to 6 decimals.
dividendQuantity.readingTip: These shares receive the following dividends in turn.

totalReturn.title: Total return
totalReturn.purpose: The gain relative to what you paid in, over the whole period, regardless of its length.
totalReturn.computation: Profit divided by the amount invested. With DCA, the latest contributions had little time to work: this return cannot be compared across durations, use the CAGR for that.
totalReturn.formula: total return = (final value − amount invested) / amount invested
totalReturn.readingTip: +15%: for every €100 paid in, €115 is left at the end.

cagr.title: CAGR (annualised return)
cagr.purpose: The average return per year, to compare strategies over different durations.
cagr.computation: {twr} The cumulative performance is then scaled to a 365.25-day calendar year, including for a period shorter than one year (extrapolation).
cagr.unit: Annual ratio displayed as a percentage.
cagr.readingTip: +7%: the portfolio grew by 7% a year on average. Over less than a year the figure is extrapolated and can look extreme.

volatility.title: Volatility
volatility.purpose: How widely the portfolio swings: the higher it is, the bumpier the ride.
volatility.computation: {twr} The engine takes the standard deviation of these daily returns (over the whole simulated history), then annualises it by multiplying by √252, the number of trading days in a year.
volatility.unit: Annual ratio displayed as a percentage.
volatility.readingTip: 15%: over a year, the return typically strays ±15% from its average.

sharpeRatio.title: Sharpe ratio
sharpeRatio.purpose: The return earned per unit of risk taken: it separates two strategies with similar returns.
sharpeRatio.computation: CAGR minus the risk-free rate, divided by the annualised volatility. Absent if volatility is zero.
sharpeRatio.readingTip: Above 1, the return pays well for the risk; below 0, the strategy did worse than the risk-free investment.

riskFreeRate.title: Risk-free rate
riskFreeRate.purpose: The return of a risk-free investment, subtracted from the CAGR in the Sharpe ratio.
riskFreeRate.computation: A fixed assumption of the engine, published with every result so you know which rate the Sharpe was computed with.
riskFreeRate.unit: Annual ratio displayed as a percentage.

maxDrawdown.title: Max drawdown
maxDrawdown.purpose: The worst loss along the way: the largest fall of the portfolio from its previous peak. It is the “worst moment” you would have had to sit through without selling.
maxDrawdown.computation: {twr} Each day, the engine compares this index with its highest value so far; the max drawdown is the deepest fall. On the result, the note in the Risk block gives the date of that peak and the panel the date of the trough.
maxDrawdown.formula:
drawdown(t) = index(t) / max index(s ≤ t) − 1
max drawdown = min drawdown(t)
maxDrawdown.unit: Ratio displayed as a percentage, always ≤ 0%. 0% means no fall.
maxDrawdown.readingTip: −12.99%: at its worst, the portfolio was worth 12.99% less than its previous best level. The closer to 0, the smoother the ride.

recovery.title: Recovery
recovery.purpose: How long it took to wipe out the worst fall (max drawdown).
recovery.computation: {twr} Recovery counts the calendar days between the peak of this index preceding the worst fall and the first day the index regains that level. With DCA, the portfolio value can rise earlier thanks to contributions: they are not taken into account. If the peak is not regained before the end of the period, the fall is not recovered.
recovery.unit: Duration in calendar days, displayed in days, months or years.
recovery.readingTip: 4 months: it took 4 months to get back to the level before the fall. “Not recovered”: the peak was not regained.

equityCurve.title: Value curve
equityCurve.purpose: Track the portfolio value day after day over the period, contributions included.
equityCurve.computation: Each trading day, value of the positions at the closing price, after any contribution and rebalancing of the day. A missing price is carried forward from the last known day.
equityCurve.readingTip: With DCA, the curve also rises at each contribution: to judge performance, read the CAGR or the drawdown, which ignore contributions.

drawdownCurve.title: Drawdown curve
drawdownCurve.purpose: See, for each day, how far the portfolio is below its previous peak.
drawdownCurve.computation: {twr} Each point is the day’s index divided by its highest value so far, minus 1.
drawdownCurve.unit: Ratio displayed as a percentage, always ≤ 0%.
drawdownCurve.readingTip: The curve touches 0% at each new peak; its lowest point is the max drawdown.

benchmark.title: Benchmark
benchmark.purpose: A point of comparison: the same savings invested 100% in a reference index (ETF), to see whether your strategy beats a passive investment.
benchmark.computation: The engine replays exactly the same contributions, on the same dates and with the same fees, on the benchmark symbol alone, without rebalancing. Its metrics are computed like those of the portfolio.
benchmark.unit: Same units as the portfolio metrics.
benchmark.readingTip: Its figures appear in the column under its symbol and as a dashed line on the value curve.

lumpSum.title: Lump sum and DCA gap
lumpSum.purpose: Answer “would it have been better to invest everything on day one?” for a monthly contribution strategy (DCA).
lumpSum.computation: The engine replays the same total paid in as a single purchase on the first day: same capital, same period, same fees, only the spread over time changes. The gap is the final value of the DCA minus that of the lump sum.
lumpSum.formula: gap = final value (DCA) − final value (lump sum)
lumpSum.readingTip: A positive gap means the DCA did better. Without a benchmark, the lump sum is the dashed curve.

totalFees.title: Fees paid
totalFees.purpose: The total cost of the orders placed during the simulation, rebalancing buys and sells included.
totalFees.computation: Sum, over every order, of the order amount multiplied by the fee rate. Fees are already deducted from the final value.

totalTrades.title: Orders
totalTrades.purpose: The number of buy and sell orders placed: an indicator of activity and therefore of fees.
totalTrades.computation: One buy per asset at each contribution (split by weights). At each rebalancing, one sell per asset above its target and one buy per asset below it, if the gap to the target is at least 0.01 in the backtest currency (one cent).

rebalanceCount.title: Rebalances
rebalanceCount.purpose: The number of times the portfolio was brought back to its target weights.
rebalanceCount.computation: On the first trading day of each period (month, quarter, year), excluding the first day, the engine sells the holdings above their target weight and buys back those below it, with no new money. The day only counts if at least one holding is above its target and another below it, by a gap of at least 0.01 in the backtest currency (one cent).

holdingQuantity.title: Quantity held
holdingQuantity.purpose: The number of shares of each asset held on the last day.
holdingQuantity.computation: Sum of the shares bought minus those sold at rebalancing. Purchases are fractional: (order amount − fees) / price.
holdingQuantity.unit: Number of shares, up to 6 decimals.

holdingValue.title: Position value
holdingValue.purpose: How much each asset weighs in the final value.
holdingValue.computation: Quantity held multiplied by the asset’s last known closing price.

tradeSide.title: Order side
tradeSide.purpose: Tell a buy from a sell.
tradeSide.computation: Buy at each contribution and for holdings below their target at rebalancing; sell for holdings above their target.

tradePrice.title: Execution price
tradePrice.purpose: The price at which the order was executed.
tradePrice.computation: Closing price, adjusted for stock splits, on the day of the contribution or rebalancing. If the asset did not trade that day, its last known price is carried forward.
tradePrice.unit: Asset price in its listing currency, without conversion.

tradeQuantity.title: Order quantity
tradeQuantity.purpose: The number of shares bought or sold.
tradeQuantity.computation: Buy: (amount − fees) / price. Sell: number of shares sold to return to the target weight.
tradeQuantity.unit: Number of shares, up to 6 decimals.

tradeAmount.title: Order amount
tradeAmount.purpose: The money committed or received by the order.
tradeAmount.computation: Buy at a contribution: share of the contribution according to the asset’s weight, fees included. Buy at a rebalancing: share of the day’s net sale proceeds, in proportion to the asset’s gap to its target, fees included. Sell: gross proceeds, quantity × price, before fees.

tradeFee.title: Order fee
tradeFee.purpose: What the order cost in fees.
tradeFee.computation: Order amount multiplied by the fee rate. Paid on a buy, withheld from the proceeds of a sell.

executionRule.title: Execution rule
executionRule.purpose: Say at what price orders are simulated, to avoid using a price that could not have been known (look-ahead bias).
executionRule.computation: Each contribution is scheduled: it is executed at the closing price of its due date.

dataSource.title: Data source
dataSource.purpose: Know where the replayed prices come from and what type of price they are.
dataSource.computation: Price provider (Yahoo Finance) and price type: close adjusted for stock splits. Recent results reinvest dividends and convert holdings to euros; older ones do not.

dataFingerprint.title: Data fingerprint
dataFingerprint.purpose: Identify exactly the prices used: two executions with the same fingerprint replayed the same data.
dataFingerprint.computation: SHA-256 fingerprint of the price series, independent of the order of symbols: it changes as soon as a price, a date or a symbol changes. Only the first characters are shown; hovering shows the full fingerprint.
dataFingerprint.readingTip: Two different results with the same fingerprint come from the parameters, not from the data.

plannedContributions.title: Planned contributions
plannedContributions.purpose: Know how many times money will enter the portfolio before launching the backtest.
plannedContributions.computation: Estimate over the working days of the period (Monday to Friday): 1 for a lump sum; with DCA, one contribution per month, the first day also receiving the initial capital. Public holidays are unknown until prices are loaded.

plannedRebalances.title: Planned rebalances
plannedRebalances.purpose: Estimate how many times the portfolio will be brought back to its target weights.
plannedRebalances.computation: Number of rebalancing periods (month, quarter, year) over the working days of the period, minus the first. High estimate: at execution, a rebalancing without a large enough gap is not counted.

completedRate.title: Success rate
completedRate.purpose: The share of your backtests whose latest execution finished with a result.
completedRate.computation: Backtests whose latest execution completed, divided by the total number of backtests (0 with no backtest).

failedRate.title: Failure rate
failedRate.purpose: The share of your backtests whose latest execution failed (missing data, engine error).
failedRate.computation: Backtests whose latest execution failed, divided by the total number of backtests (0 with no backtest).

executionDuration.title: Execution duration
executionDuration.purpose: The calculation time of the latest execution, from its start by the engine to its result.
executionDuration.computation: Difference between the end time and the start time of the execution (or its creation time if it has no start time). Absent until the execution is finished.

comparisonDelta.title: Gap A − B
comparisonDelta.purpose: Measure at a glance by how much A does better or worse than B on each metric.
comparisonDelta.computation: A’s metric minus B’s same metric. Green if the gap favours A (more return, less volatility, a shallower drawdown), red if it is unfavourable, neutral if zero.
comparisonDelta.unit: Percentage points for ratios (pp), no unit for the Sharpe.
comparisonDelta.readingTip: +4.4 pp of CAGR: A earns 4.4% more per year than B.

investmentMode.title: Investment mode
investmentMode.purpose: Choose how money enters the portfolio: all on the first day, or through regular contributions (DCA).
investmentMode.computation: Lump sum: the initial capital is invested on the first day. Monthly contributions (DCA): the first day receives the initial capital and the first monthly contribution, then one contribution on the first trading day of each following month.
investmentMode.readingTip: With DCA, the result also shows what the same total invested in one go would have produced.

allocation.title: Assets and weights
allocation.purpose: Define the target split of the portfolio among its assets.
allocation.computation: Each contribution is split among the assets according to their weight; the weights add up to 100%. Rebalancing brings the portfolio back to these weights.

feeRate.title: Fee per order
feeRate.purpose: Simulate brokerage cost, which reduces performance on every buy and sell.
feeRate.computation: Percentage charged on the amount of each order, buy or sell.

rebalanceFrequency.title: Rebalancing
rebalanceFrequency.purpose: Regularly bring the portfolio back to its target weights, so the asset that rose the most does not take over.
rebalanceFrequency.computation: On the first trading day of each period, the engine sells the holdings above their target and buys back those below it, with no new money. Each order pays fees. “None”: never sells.

price.title: Price
price.computation: Market price of the current session, or closing price if the market is closed, provided by Yahoo Finance.

change24h.title: 24h change
change24h.purpose: How much the asset has moved since the last close.
change24h.computation: Change of the current price relative to the previous close, provided by Yahoo Finance.

volume24h.title: 24h volume
volume24h.purpose: Activity on the asset: a high volume signals heavy trading, hence a more reliable price.
volume24h.computation: Number of shares traded during the current session, provided by Yahoo Finance.
volume24h.unit: Number of shares, abbreviated (K, M, B).

trend.title: Trend
trend.purpose: See at a glance how the price moved over the last 24 hours.
trend.computation: Hourly closing prices over the last 24 hours; green if the change is positive or zero, red if it is negative.

priceChart.title: Price chart
priceChart.purpose: Follow the asset’s price over the chosen period.
priceChart.computation: Closing prices provided by Yahoo Finance, one point per interval (5 min over 1 day, 1 h over 1 week, 1 day over 1 month, 1 week over 1 year, 1 month beyond). An interval without a close (market closed) is omitted.

rollingWindow.title: Rolling windows
rollingWindow.purpose: Answers “how much would I have lost entering at the wrong time?”: the return obtained by entering on each trading day and leaving 1, 3 or 5 years later.
rollingWindow.computation: {twr} For each start day, the return is that of the index between that day and the first trading day one, three or five years later, scaled to one year; starts without a full window are ignored.
rollingWindow.formula: Annualised return = (index at window end / index at start)^(1 / years) − 1
rollingWindow.unit: Annual ratio displayed as a percentage; negative share = share of windows with a negative return.
rollingWindow.readingTip: Worst −4.1%/yr over 3 years: entering at the worst time would have returned −4.1% a year for 3 years.

medianCagr.title: Median CAGR
medianCagr.purpose: The typical annualised return of the strategy, across all start dates.
medianCagr.computation: Median of the CAGRs of the batch’s starts (each backtest’s CAGR, see its definition).
medianCagr.unit: Annual ratio displayed as a percentage; the worst–best gap is in percentage points.
medianCagr.readingTip: A narrow worst–best gap means the strategy is not very sensitive to the entry date.

worstStart.title: Worst start
worstStart.purpose: The entry date that gave the lowest annualised return.
worstStart.computation: The batch start with the lowest CAGR, over the period from its start to the common end.
worstStart.unit: Annual ratio displayed as a percentage.
worstStart.readingTip: Starts have different durations: only the (annualised) CAGR is comparable.

worstWindow.title: Worst window
worstWindow.purpose: The worst return obtained by staying invested for the window’s duration, whatever the entry date.
worstWindow.computation: Lowest annualised return among the 3-year windows of the earliest start, one window per entry trading day.
worstWindow.unit: Annual ratio displayed as a percentage.
worstWindow.readingTip: The entry day shown is the one of the least favourable window.

negativeWindows.title: Negative windows
negativeWindows.purpose: How often an entry, held for the window’s duration, would have ended in a loss.
negativeWindows.computation: Share of rolling windows whose return is strictly negative, on the earliest start.
negativeWindows.unit: Ratio displayed as a percentage of windows.
negativeWindows.readingTip: 8%: out of 100 possible entry days, 8 would have lost money over the chosen duration.

riskVolatility.title: Volatility (risk)
riskVolatility.purpose: How much the portfolio at target weights, and each asset, swings.
riskVolatility.computation: The risk engine takes daily returns in euros (FX included) on the trading days shared by every asset, weighted at constant target weights, then annualizes their standard deviation by √252. Contributions and rebalancing play no part.
riskVolatility.unit: Annual ratio shown as a percentage.
riskVolatility.readingTip: It may differ from the result volatility, which follows the actually simulated portfolio.

valueAtRisk.title: Historical VaR 95%
valueAtRisk.purpose: The loss of a bad day: 1 day in 20 was worse in history.
valueAtRisk.computation: Daily portfolio returns at target weights are sorted; with n returns and k = ⌈5% × n⌉, the VaR is the k-th smallest.
valueAtRisk.unit: One-day ratio shown as a percentage (negative = loss).
valueAtRisk.readingTip: −1.4%: one day in twenty, the portfolio lost more than 1.4%.

expectedShortfall.title: Historical CVaR 95%
expectedShortfall.purpose: The average loss of the worst days, beyond the VaR.
expectedShortfall.computation: Mean of the k smallest daily returns, with the same k as the VaR.
expectedShortfall.unit: One-day ratio shown as a percentage (negative = loss).
expectedShortfall.readingTip: Always lower than or equal to the VaR: it tells how much a very bad day costs.

concentration.title: Concentration
concentration.purpose: Measures whether capital rests on few assets.
concentration.computation: Herfindahl index of target weights: sum of squared weights. Effective assets = 1 / HHI; the large value is the maximum weight.
concentration.unit: HHI: ratio from 0 to 1; effective assets: number.

correlation.title: Correlation
correlation.purpose: Tells whether two assets rise and fall together.
correlation.computation: Pearson correlation of daily returns in euros, on shared trading days.
correlation.readingTip: Close to 1: little diversification; negative: one cushions the other.

riskContribution.title: Risk contribution
riskContribution.purpose: Each asset’s share of portfolio volatility, to compare with its weight.
riskContribution.computation: Share of portfolio variance carried by the asset at target weights: wᵢ (Σw)ᵢ / σ². Shares sum to 100%.
riskContribution.readingTip: An asset that is 30% of capital can carry 44% of the risk.

projectionPercentile.title: Projection percentiles
projectionPercentile.purpose: The range of values the portfolio could reach: P10 an unfavourable scenario, median the central one, P90 a favourable one.
projectionPercentile.computation: The risk engine draws thousands of paths by resampling blocks of days from the common price history, at constant target weights, then reads the percentiles of their value at each horizon. Only the percentiles are stored.
projectionPercentile.unit: Amount in euros, on the backtest's starting capital.
projectionPercentile.readingTip: P10: 9 scenarios out of 10 do better. Median: a coin flip. P90: 1 scenario out of 10 does better.

projectionLossProbability.title: Probability of loss
projectionLossProbability.purpose: The share of scenarios that end below the invested amount at the chosen horizon.
projectionLossProbability.computation: Share of the paths whose value is strictly below the starting capital at that horizon.
projectionLossProbability.readingTip: Computed on historical scenarios, not a promise: the future can fall outside this range.

bondPrice.title: Discounted price
bondPrice.purpose: What the bond is worth today: the sum of its future cash flows brought back to today.
bondPrice.computation: Each cash flow (coupon, then the principal at the last date) is multiplied by its discount factor; the price is the sum of these present values.
bondPrice.unit: Euros, for the entered face value.
bondPrice.readingTip: A price below the face value means the discount rate is above the coupon.

macaulayDuration.title: Macaulay duration
macaulayDuration.purpose: The average time, in years, after which you get the bond back, discounted cash flows included.
macaulayDuration.computation: Average of the payment years weighted by the present value of each cash flow, divided by the price.
macaulayDuration.readingTip: For a zero-coupon bond it equals the maturity exactly.

modifiedDuration.title: Modified duration
modifiedDuration.purpose: The price sensitivity to rates: how much it drops when rates rise.
modifiedDuration.computation: Macaulay duration divided by (1 + rate). A 1-point rise in rates moves the price by about −modified duration × 1%.
modifiedDuration.unit: Years; the price change shown is a ratio displayed as a percentage.
modifiedDuration.readingTip: First-order approximation: reliable for small rate moves.

discountFactor.title: Discount factor
discountFactor.purpose: What one euro received at the payment date is worth today.
discountFactor.computation: 1 divided by (1 + rate) raised to the number of years (annual compound discounting, 365 basis).
discountFactor.unit: Ratio without unit, below 1 for a positive rate.
discountFactor.readingTip: The later the payment date, the smaller the factor.

interpolatedRate.title: Rate used
interpolatedRate.purpose: The discount rate applied to every cash flow of the bond.
interpolatedRate.computation: Entered rate (flat rate), or the US curve rate read at the bond maturity by linear interpolation between the two points around it. Outside the curve, the calculation fails: no extrapolation.
interpolatedRate.unit: Annual ratio shown as a percentage.
interpolatedRate.readingTip: The curve is American, in dollars; there is no free and reliable euro curve.

serviceState.title: Service state
serviceState.purpose: Tells whether a service can work and, if not, whether the service itself or one of its dependencies is failing.
serviceState.computation: core-backend calls the /readiness probe of every other service with a 2 s timeout, and runs its own checks (database, Kafka) without a network call. 200 response: operational. 503 response: degraded, the service answers but a dependency (database, Kafka or Yahoo) is down. No response within the timeout, refused connection or unreadable response: offline. The summary cards count the services in each state.
serviceState.unit: State among operational, degraded and offline; numbers of services.
serviceState.readingTip: A degraded service is still running: the “Down” line on its card names the dependency to fix.

probeLatency.title: Probe latency
probeLatency.purpose: Spots a slow service before it exceeds the timeout and goes offline.
probeLatency.computation: Time measured by core-backend between sending the /readiness call and receiving the response, rounded to the millisecond; for core-backend, the duration of its own checks. Missing when the service is offline.

optionPrice.title: Option price
optionPrice.purpose: What the right to buy (call) or sell (put) a stock at the strike price at expiry is worth today.
optionPrice.computation: European Black-Scholes model with continuous dividend: discounted expected payoff at expiry, under constant volatility.
optionPrice.unit: Currency of the underlying, per share.
optionPrice.readingTip: Time value = price − intrinsic value: what the market pays for the remaining uncertainty.

optionBreakEven.title: Break-even
optionBreakEven.purpose: The final stock price from which buying the option pays back the premium.
optionBreakEven.computation: Strike + premium for a call, strike − premium for a put.
optionBreakEven.readingTip: Below (call) or above (put) the break-even, the purchase loses part of the premium; the maximum loss is the premium.

callPutParity.title: Call-put parity
callPutParity.purpose: Consistency check: a call and a put with the same strike and expiry are linked by an exact relation.
callPutParity.computation: Call − Put must equal the discounted spot net of dividends minus the discounted strike; the gap measures what the engine does not respect.
callPutParity.readingTip: A gap of zero (to 6 decimals) means the two prices are consistent with each other.

optionVolatility.title: Volatility used
optionVolatility.purpose: The assumed yearly amplitude of price moves: the parameter that moves an option price the most.
optionVolatility.computation: Prefilled with the standard deviation of daily log returns over 1 year, times √252; you can change it.
optionVolatility.readingTip: It is a past volatility, not an implied one: the options market may expect another.

impliedVolatility.title: Implied volatility
impliedVolatility.purpose: The volatility the market “pays”: the one that, plugged into Black-Scholes, gives back the option’s quoted price.
impliedVolatility.computation: Black-Scholes inversion by bisection between 1% and 300% on the mid price (bid + ask) / 2, within 1e-6 on the price. Never copied from Yahoo.
impliedVolatility.unit: Annual ratio, shown as a percentage.
impliedVolatility.readingTip: The higher it is, the more movement the market expects; compare it with historical volatility.

historicalVolatility30.title: 30-day historical volatility
historicalVolatility30.purpose: What actually happened recently, to compare with what the market expects.
historicalVolatility30.computation: Standard deviation of daily log returns over the last 30 trading days, annualised by √252.
historicalVolatility30.unit: Annual ratio, shown as a percentage; the gap to ATM IV is in points.
historicalVolatility30.readingTip: ATM IV above it: the market expects more movement than the recent past.

volatilitySmile.title: Volatility smile
volatilitySmile.purpose: Shows that implied volatility depends on the strike, while Black-Scholes assumes it constant.
volatilitySmile.computation: For each expiry, implied volatility of the kept out-of-the-money contracts: puts below spot, calls above.
volatilitySmile.readingTip: A curve rising toward low strikes: the market pays more for downside protection.

quoteFilter.title: Quote quality filter
quoteFilter.purpose: Drops unusable quotes before any calculation, and counts them.
quoteFilter.computation: Dropped: empty bid and ask, no mid price (only one of the two at zero), implied volatility outside [1%, 300%].
quoteFilter.readingTip: Many discarded contracts point to an illiquid chain, not to an engine error.

monteCarloPrice.title: Monte Carlo price
monteCarloPrice.purpose: The price of the option obtained by simulation, where no formula exists.
monteCarloPrice.computation: Thousands of price paths are drawn (geometric Brownian motion, drift r − q); the price is the average payoff at maturity, discounted at the risk-free rate.
monteCarloPrice.readingTip: Same seed: same price. The price is an estimator: read it with its standard error.

standardError.title: Standard error (SE)
standardError.purpose: The precision of the simulated price: the smaller it is, the more reliable the price.
standardError.computation: Standard deviation of the discounted payoffs divided by the square root of the number of paths.
standardError.readingTip: Four times more paths halve the error. A price within 3 SE of the formula is validated.

barrierOption.title: Barrier option
barrierOption.purpose: An option that disappears (knock-out) or only exists (knock-in) if the price touches a level.
barrierOption.computation: The barrier is monitored at every daily close of every path. On the same paths, knock-out + knock-in = vanilla option.
barrierOption.readingTip: A knock-out is cheaper than the vanilla: it can disappear. It is the building block of structured products.

monteCarloPaths.title: Paths
monteCarloPaths.purpose: The number of simulated price scenarios used to estimate the price.
monteCarloPaths.computation: Integer from 10,000 to 1,000,000; the draw seed is fixed, so the result can be replayed.
monteCarloPaths.readingTip: The larger it is, the lower the standard error, at the cost of a longer computation.

greekDelta.title: Delta
greekDelta.purpose: How much the option price moves when the underlying moves by 1.
greekDelta.computation: Derivative of the Black-Scholes price with respect to spot, at the mid price.
greekDelta.unit: No unit (call between 0 and 1, put between −1 and 0).
greekDelta.readingTip: A delta of 0.5: the option gains about 0.5 for +1 on the underlying.

greekGamma.title: Gamma
greekGamma.purpose: How fast delta changes with spot.
greekGamma.computation: Second derivative of the price with respect to spot.
greekGamma.readingTip: High near the money and near expiry.

greekVega.title: Vega
greekVega.purpose: Sensitivity of the price to volatility.
greekVega.computation: Derivative of the price with respect to volatility, expressed for +1 point.
greekVega.readingTip: A vega of 0.9: +1 volatility point adds about 0.9 to the price.

greekTheta.title: Theta
greekTheta.purpose: What the passing of time costs the buyer.
greekTheta.computation: Derivative of the price with respect to time, per calendar day.
greekTheta.readingTip: Negative for a purchase: the option loses value every day.

greekRho.title: Rho
greekRho.purpose: Sensitivity of the price to the risk-free rate.
greekRho.computation: Derivative of the price with respect to the rate, expressed for +1 point.
greekRho.readingTip: Positive for a call, negative for a put.

optionFinalSpot.title: Final price
optionFinalSpot.purpose: The underlying price assumed at expiry, for which the row computes the option's outcome.
optionFinalSpot.computation: Grid of 21 evenly spaced points, from 70% of the lower of spot and strike to 130% of the higher.

optionPayoff.title: Payoff at expiry
optionPayoff.purpose: What the option pays at expiry for this final price, before deducting the premium paid.
optionPayoff.computation: Call: max(final price − strike, 0). Put: max(strike − final price, 0).
optionPayoff.formula: Call = max(S − K, 0) · Put = max(K − S, 0)
optionPayoff.readingTip: Never negative: an option buyer loses at worst the premium.

optionNet.title: Net result
optionNet.purpose: Gain or loss of buying the option, premium included, if the final price is the row's.
optionNet.computation: Payoff at expiry minus the Black-Scholes model premium, undiscounted.
optionNet.unit: Underlying currency, per share. Green: gain, red: loss.
optionNet.readingTip: Negative while the payoff does not cover the premium; zero at the break-even.

quoteBidAsk.title: Bid and ask
quoteBidAsk.purpose: Quoted market prices: the bid is the highest price a buyer offers, the ask the lowest a seller wants.
quoteBidAsk.computation: Read as quoted by Yahoo Finance, no calculation.
quoteBidAsk.readingTip: A wide bid-ask spread points to an illiquid contract.

midPrice.title: Mid price
midPrice.purpose: The price kept for the contract: the starting point of the implied volatility and Greeks calculation.
midPrice.computation: Average of bid and ask. Zero, the quote is discarded.

yahooVolatility.title: Yahoo implied volatility
yahooVolatility.purpose: The implied volatility supplied with the quote, shown to compare with the engine's.
yahooVolatility.computation: Read as received from Yahoo Finance, never used in a calculation.
yahooVolatility.unit: Annual ratio, shown as a percentage.
yahooVolatility.readingTip: A gap with the engine IV comes from the mid price and Black-Scholes assumptions, not from an error.

structuredFairValue.title: Fair value
structuredFairValue.purpose: What the product is worth today, brick by brick, regardless of the price it is sold at.
structuredFairValue.computation: Sum of the bricks: discounted zero-coupon or bond, plus the option bought, minus the option sold. The autocallable is simulated (Monte Carlo, fixed seed).
structuredFairValue.unit: Euros, and share of the nominal.

structuredMargin.title: Structurer's margin
structuredMargin.purpose: What the seller of the product earns: the gap between what the client pays and what the product is worth.
structuredMargin.computation: Client price (the nominal, 100 %) minus the fair value. The issuer's hedging and funding costs are not modelled.
structuredMargin.unit: Euros, and share of the client price.
structuredMargin.readingTip: A negative margin means the promised coupon exceeds what the fair value funds.

structuredParticipation.title: Participation
structuredParticipation.purpose: The share of the underlying's rise the client receives on top of the guaranteed capital.
structuredParticipation.computation: Option budget (nominal minus zero-coupon minus margin) divided by the price of a call at the chosen strike.
structuredParticipation.readingTip: The higher the guarantee, the smaller the option budget, and the participation with it.

structuredOptionBudget.title: Option budget
structuredOptionBudget.purpose: What is left to buy the call once the guaranteed capital is funded and the margin taken.
structuredOptionBudget.computation: Nominal minus the zero-coupon that returns the guarantee, minus the structuring margin.

structuredRecallProbability.title: Recall probability
structuredRecallProbability.purpose: The share of scenarios where the product is redeemed early, on a given observation date.
structuredRecallProbability.computation: Share of simulated paths whose level is above the recall level on that date, without having been before.
structuredRecallProbability.readingTip: The maturity line gives the share of paths that reach the end without being recalled.

structuredProtectionBarrier.title: Protection barrier
structuredProtectionBarrier.purpose: The underlying level below which the capital is no longer returned at maturity.
structuredProtectionBarrier.computation: Observed at maturity only: below the barrier, the client receives the nominal times the final level.
structuredProtectionBarrier.readingTip: A lower barrier protects more capital: the fair value rises.

structuredRecallLevel.title: Recall level
structuredRecallLevel.purpose: The underlying level from which the product is redeemed early, with its accumulated coupons.
structuredRecallLevel.computation: Observed every year: a level above the threshold repays the nominal plus the accumulated coupon and ends the product.
